title: Sustainable Development and Planning
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course critically examines the transformation of conventional urban planning and land development processes into sustainable, inclusive, and resilient systems. It is structured in two integrated parts:Part I: Urban Development and Planning FrameworksStudents will explore the legal, administrative, and institutional structures that shape land development in Hong Kong and other global cities. Topics include zoning regulations, land use policy, environmental impact assessment, and governance mechanisms. Comparative case studies from cities such as Hong Kong, Singapore, Stockholm, New York, and Shenzhen will be used to highlight diverse planning models and their implications for sustainability.Part II: Planning for Sustainable Urban FuturesBuilding on foundational knowledge, students will engage with international frameworks such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the New Urban Agenda to reimagine planning processes. Emphasis will be placed on climate-resilient infrastructure, adaptation planning, decarbonization, participatory planning, spatial justice, and circular urban systems that promote resource efficiency and regenerative design. Students will apply spatial planning tools (e.g. GIS, urban simulation, or data visualization) and policy analysis to propose sustainable interventions tailored to urban challenges in different contexts.
outcome: After taking this course, students will be able to: Identify and explain key legal, institutional, and environmental frameworks that shape urban planning and land development in Hong Kong and other global cities. Apply and adapt international sustainability frameworks, such as the SDGs and the New Urban Agenda, to local planning contexts through spatial analysis and policy evaluation. Compare and contrast diverse urban planning models and development strategies across global cities, evaluating their effectiveness in promoting sustainable outcomes. Critically assess the role of planning tools (e.g. GIS, urban simulation, data visualization) in diagnosing urban challenges and designing sustainable interventions. Reflect on and evaluate ethical dimensions of planning practice, including spatial justice, housing equity, and inclusive stakeholder engagement. Synthesize and generalize interdisciplinary concepts to formulate integrated planning strategies that address climate resilience, decarbonization, and circular urban systems.
syllabus: Part I: Urban Development and Planning Frameworks Introduction to sustainable urban planning Legal and institutional frameworks in Hong Kong Global planning systems and comparative models Zoning, land use, and development control Environmental impact assessment and urban governance Urban growth, land markets, and planning challenges Planning ethics and professional practice Part II: Planning for Sustainable Urban Futures Sustainable development goals and the New Urban Agenda Climate-resilient infrastructure and adaptive planning Decarbonization and low-carbon urban design Participatory planning and stakeholder engagement Spatial justice, housing equity, and mobility access Circular urban systems and resource efficiencyIntegrated planning strategies and future directions

title: Territorial Spatial Planning Practice in China
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course provides a practical introduction to China's Territorial Spatial Planning System, Case studies, and the latest planning policies and measures. The content covers: the evolution of the territorial spatial planning system; the basis, content, and case studies of macro, medium, and micro-level planning; special planning; spatial planning databases and cutting-edge practices, as well as the latest policies and issues (including "Beautiful China," low-carbon cities, sponge cities, resilient cities, smart city, high-speed rail and transit-oriented development, rural revitalization, urban renewal, and urban design).
outcome: After taking this course, students should be able to: Understand the basic framework of Territorial Spatial Planning (TSP) in China; Understand the basic planning standards and guidelines in planning practice in China; Compare the Hong Kong planning system and practices with Chinese mainland; Find planning information and keep track of the planning policy, latest planning issues in Chinese mainland and critically understand the gist of the policy and issues;  Build up basic professional skills in site and project analysis; Build up multi-dimensional skills and confidence in planning communication.

title: Planning Laws and Practice
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: There are various perspectives on understanding the legal system as it applies to town planning and practice in different contexts. In this course, the primary focus will be on development controls related to land use and the preparation of statutory town plans. It is also essential to adopt a multi-dimensional approach when handling planning matters.The field of planning has evolved significantly over time. Today, three-dimensional spatial planning faces a range of emerging challenges, including broad issues such as nurturing biodiversity, reducing carbon emissions, and addressing socio-spatial and environmental justice, as well as localized concerns such as urban design, air ventilation, landscaping proposals, and traffic arrangements. Consequently, this specialized subject must remain current to equip professionals with the knowledge and skills needed to understand and effectively apply contemporary best planning practices.
outcome: By the end of the program, graduates will be able to: Address planning matters subject to the social, physical, and economic development of urban and rural environments in Hong Kong, prioritizing the best interests of the community; Meet the full membership (MHKIP) requirements of the Hong Kong Institute of Planners; Demonstrate awareness of the role of town planning in strategic planning and planning & engineering (P&E) studies in both public and private sector contexts; Understand the key tripartite relationship in the development process among town planning, lease control, and building planning regulations; Possess the knowledge and skill set necessary to give employers confidence in their ability to practice town planning effectively, with particular reference to Hong Kong; Promote cooperation and mutual understanding with related disciplines—such as traffic engineering, environmental management, and landscaping—within the development process in Hong Kong; and Maintain a sustainable and professional attitude, applying good practices to enhance the professionalism of town planning.

title: Urban and Regional Economics
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and analytical frameworks of urban and regional economics. Students will learn how economic forces shape cities and regions through the behaviour of households, firms, and governments. Topics include location theory, land rent and land-use models, agglomeration economies, labour and housing markets, transport accessibility, and regional development. The course emphasises the application of microeconomic principles and quantitative tools to understand spatial patterns, evaluate policy interventions, and support evidence-based urban and regional planning.
outcome: After taking this course, students are expected to: Understand basic microeconomic concepts as tools to explain the location choices of households and firms. Understand key theories of urban and regional economics, including location theory, agglomeration economies, land rent, and spatial equilibrium. Analyse the economic forces shaping cities and regions, such as labour markets, housing markets, transport accessibility, and innovation clusters. Apply quantitative and spatial analytical tools to evaluate urban economic patterns and policy interventions.
syllabus: Lecture 1: Introduction to Urban and Regional Economics  Overview of the field, scope, and relevance to urban planning and policy.   Lecture 2: Basic Microeconomic Principles  Microeconomics, market equilibrium, and welfare concepts.   Lecture 3: Location Theory, Location Models  Spatial distribution of economic activities; location decisions of households and firms.   Lecture 4: Land Rent and Urban Land-Use Models  Alonso–Muth–Mills framework and implications for land-use planning and housing markets.   Lecture 5: Agglomeration Economies and Urban Productivity  Economies of scale, knowledge spillovers, and innovation clusters.   Lecture 6: Urban Labour Markets and Housing Markets  Wage, housing markets, and commuting patterns.   Lecture 7: Transport Accessibility and Urban Form  Economic effects of transport infrastructure and land-use interactions.   Lecture 8: Regional Economic Growth and Spatial Disparities  Regional convergence/divergence, core–periphery models, and globalisation.   Lecture 9: Urban Public Finance and Urban Development  Public finance, land value capture, and fiscal tools in urban development.   Lecture 10: Policy for Sustainable Urban and Regional Development  Government programmes, policy and interventions.   Lecture 11: Data and Indicators for Urban and Regional Analysis  Key data sources (e.g. census, land use, economic and spatial datasets), basic econometric tools, and interpretation of urban economic indicators.   Lecture 12: Innovation, Knowledge Economies, and the Digital City  The role of technology, innovation ecosystems, and digital transformation in reshaping urban and regional economies.
recommended_readings: McCann, P. (2013). Urban and Regional Economics. Routledge. Edwards, M. (2017). Regional and Urban Economics and Economic Development: Theory and Methods. Routledge. Mankiw, N. G. (2021). Principles of Microeconomics (10th ed.). Cengage.

title: Research Methods in Urban Planning
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: "Research Methods in Urban Planning" provides students with a comprehensive understanding of various qualitative and quantitative research techniques essential for analyzing, designing, and evaluating urban environments. Through critical examination of data collection, analysis methods, and case studies, students will develop the skills to conduct rigorous and evidence-based research tailored to urban planning challenges. Emphasis will be placed on integrating theoretical frameworks with practical applications to address complex urban issues.Students will also learn to critically assess the strengths and limitations of different research methodologies and ethical considerations relevant to urban planning related research. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to design and implement independent research projects, effectively communicate findings, and contribute to informed policy-making and planning practice.
outcome: Critically evaluate a broad range of qualitative and quantitative research methods relevant to urban planning. Design and develop rigorous research proposals that address complex urban planning issues using appropriate methodologies. Apply advanced data collection and analysis techniques to investigate urban phenomena and interpret findings within planning contexts. Integrate theoretical frameworks with empirical research to formulate evidence-based urban planning strategies and solutions. Assess ethical considerations and challenges in urban planning research and ensure adherence to professional standards. Communicate research outcomes effectively to diverse audiences, including policymakers, practitioners, and academic peers.

title: Spatial Planning Studio I
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This studio aims to equip students with basic spatial planning and design skills. Students will learn the spatial planning process from baseline review to formulation of spatial planning framework and development proposals. Various planning skills, including community auditing, public engagement methods, digital techniques, visualization, GIS, place-making and design thinking approaches will be introduced with real-life examples in planning practice. Students will be provided with opportunities to practise various skills to understand their application in different spatial contexts.
outcome: After taking this course, students are expected to: develop proficiency in mastering various spatial planning and design skills understand the application of spatial planning skills in real-world planning practice, and gain teamwork experience which fosters critical thinking skills and collaborative learning

title: Spatial Planning Studio II
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This studio encourages students to use their skills to conduct spatial planning and design exercises at different geographical levels, ranging from regional development strategy to community and neighbourhood planning. Students will be provided with opportunities to engage different stakeholders to develop a sustainable planning strategy which integrates social inclusion, economic vitality and environmental protection.
outcome: After taking this course, students are expected to: apply spatial planning skills to develop planning and development strategies at the community and regional levels, Understand the complex relationships between spatial planning and enhancing environmental, economic and social sustainability  engage different stakeholders and balance their interests in the planning process, and gain teamwork experience which fosters critical thinking skills and collaborative learning
syllabus: By conducting projects in different spatial scales, students will be able to develop spatial planning strategies that improve neighbourhoods with socio-economic vitality and environmental sustainability.Stage 1: Contextualization in the regional context  (3 weeks) Site visit and research on the regional context in terms of demographic, socio-economic, environmental, land use, infrastructural and institutional dimensions Discussion workshops on the regional planning and development issuesStage 2: Community profiling and envisioning  (3 weeks) Community audit and needs assessment to understand, map and interpret the community’s urban fabric, social network and community resources  Stakeholders’ workshop to envision and identify planning opportunities and challenges Stage 3: Formulation of planning principles, design concepts and spatial planning framework (4 weeks) Based on Stage 2 and Stage 3 reviews, formulate a spatial planning framework Critique / mid-term review on the conceptual spatial frameworkStage 4: Generation of planning options and improvement strategies (4 weeks) Generate planning options at community or neighbourhood levels Final presentation

title: Values in Spatial Planning
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course aims to engage students to reflect on value issues in the planning process. It explores competing understandings of how planning should be conducted, what goals planning should achieve, and why planning should be practised in particular ways. It encourages students to examine the value implications of various planning theories for government, the market and civil society, and to develop and justify their own value positions in the planning process.

title: Urban AI
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course introduces the emerging field of Urban Artificial Intelligence (Urban AI) and its applications in sustainable urban planning. Students will learn fundamental programming skills in Python, key machine learning techniques, and AI-driven methods for analysing spatial, social media, and street view image data. The course integrates theory and practice—covering smart city concepts, big data analytics, and human–AI interactions—to equip students with the analytical and critical thinking skills needed to address complex urban challenges. Through individual essays and group projects, students will apply AI tools to real-world planning and policy issues.

title: Smart Sustainable Planning for Human Flourishing
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course introduces students to the concept and practice of smart cities. Students are encouraged to explore with different stakeholders to understand what smart initiatives and processes are essential for the well-being of planet, place and people.

title: Socio-economic and Environmental Valuation
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course aims to introduce valuation techniques that go beyond traditional cost-benefit analysis to enhance students’ capability to assess social and environmental values in the development and planning process. These include social value impact assessment and ecosystem service value assessment.

title: Sustainable Planning Laboratory
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This Laboratory provides a platform for students to explore planning concepts and practices that promote ecological, human-centric, smart, green and resilient urbanism in a concrete context. Using a combination of case study-based lectures and interactive tutorials, students develop a speculative and research-based spatial planning concept which integrates various urban systems. By referring to international and regional cases of innovative planning, students explore how land-use planning, road networks and transport nodes, and urban green networks shape environmental, economic and social sustainability.

title: Sustainable Urban Planning Thesis
requirements: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
description: This course is the capstone of the Master of Science in Sustainable Urban Planning programme. Each student is required to undertake an independent research thesis under the supervision of an academic advisor. The thesis should demonstrate the student’s ability to integrate planning theories, research methods, and professional knowledge to address real-world urban challenges. Through this process, students develop analytical, critical, and reflective skills essential for professional practice and research in sustainable urban planning.
